Site.description: Free browser tools for images, in batches of up to 20: resize with locked aspect ratio or a social preset, crop to preset ratios or a circle, rotate and flip, compress by quality or target size, convert between JPEG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, TIFF, SVG and ICO favicons, stamp a text or logo watermark, inspect EXIF and GPS metadata, combine images into a multi-page PDF, and merge several PDFs into one.
Site.footerBlurb: Focused tools for everyday image work — no account, no queue, no watermarks. Uploads are processed in memory and never stored.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.metaDescription: What happens to the images you upload: processed in memory on the server, never stored, metadata stripped by default.
Privacy.intro: The short version: your images are processed in memory and never stored.

processing.title: Where your images are processed
processing.p1: Processing happens on the server, not in your browser. When you press the button, the file is sent over HTTPS to a Server Action, decoded in memory by sharp, and the result comes straight back in the response.
processing.p2: Nothing is written to disk, no database, no object storage, no queue. Once the request finishes, the memory holding your image is released. There is no copy left to download, index or share, and no URL that points at your file.

notCollected.title: What is not collected
notCollected.p1: No accounts, no sign-up, no email address. There is no upload history, because nothing is kept to build one from.
notCollected.p2: The only thing stored in your browser is your light/dark theme choice, in localStorage. No tracking cookies are set.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.p1: The site uses Vercel Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights, which record anonymous page views and page-load timings. They see which tool page was opened and how fast it rendered — never the images, filenames or settings you use.
analytics.p2: If processing fails, the error itself is logged to the server console so the bug can be fixed. The image is not part of that log.

metadata.title: Metadata in your files
metadata.p1: Every tool bakes the EXIF orientation into the pixels, so a photo can never come out rotated after its orientation tag is dropped.
metadata.p2: Compress always removes all metadata (EXIF, GPS coordinates, ICC profile, XMP). Resize, crop, rotate, watermark and convert remove it by default and offer a switch to keep it — worth remembering that GPS coordinates travel inside photos taken on a phone.
metadata.p3: The metadata tool exists to show you exactly that: it reads the EXIF, camera, GPS and color profile out of a file and reports them back to you, in the same in-memory request as every other tool, then hands you a clean copy if you want one.

limits.title: Limits
limits.p1: Uploads are capped at {maxFileSize} and 100 megapixels per image. These limits exist to keep the server responsive, not to collect anything.

Compress.metaDescription: Reduce image file size with adjustable quality or a target size, one image or a batch of 20. Metadata is always stripped.
Compress.heading: Compress
Compress.intro: Reduce file size with adjustable quality, or aim for a target size like 500 KB. Drop in up to 20 images at once. EXIF, ICC and XMP metadata are always removed.
Compress.qualityHint: Target output quality: 1 gives the smallest file, 100 the best quality.
Compress.targetSizeHint: Picks the highest quality that fits under the target. Dimensions stay the same — if the target is unreachable, resize the image first.
Compress.pngNote: PNG output is written as an 8-bit palette image — that's where most of the saving comes from. Ideal for screenshots, logos and flat graphics; on photos it can show visible banding, so convert those to JPEG or WEBP instead.
Compress.metadataNote: All metadata (EXIF, GPS location, ICC profile, XMP) is stripped from the output.

Resize.metaDescription: Resize JPEG, PNG, WEBP or AVIF images to exact pixel dimensions, one or twenty at a time, with optional rotation.
Resize.heading: Resize
Resize.intro: Set exact pixel dimensions and optionally rotate the image. Lock the aspect ratio to keep proportions intact; the same box applies to every image in a batch.
Resize.presetHint: Fills the exact box a platform expects: the fit switches to cover, so the image is scaled up and the overflow is cropped, centered.
Resize.noEnlargeHint: Leaves the image at its original size when it is already smaller than the target — upscaling only adds blur.
Resize.batchNote: Every image is resized to the same target box with the fit above.

Rotate.metaDescription: Rotate JPEG, PNG, WEBP or AVIF images by 90°, 180°, 270° or any angle, and mirror or flip them — up to 20 at a time.
Rotate.heading: Rotate & Flip
Rotate.intro: Turn a photo the right way up, or tilt it by any angle you type. Free angles expose the corners, which get filled with the color you choose — or left transparent.
Rotate.flipHint: Flips are applied after the rotation.
Rotate.cornersHint: An angle that isn't a multiple of 90° exposes corners.
Rotate.cornersTransparent: They stay transparent — except in JPEG, which has no alpha channel and falls back to the color below.
Rotate.cornersFilled: They are filled with the color below.
Rotate.previewHint: Approximate preview of the first image. The download is rendered at full size, with the canvas grown to fit the rotation.
Rotate.nothingToDo: Pick an angle or a flip

Compare.metaDescription: See what one image weighs as JPEG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF at the same quality, side by side, and download the smallest.
Compare.heading: Compare formats
Compare.intro: Encode one image to every format at the same quality and see which comes out smallest, before you commit to one.
Compare.qualityHint: Every format is encoded at this same setting, which is what makes the sizes comparable. The numbers match what the Compress tool produces.
Compare.encodedAt: Encoded at quality {quality} from a {size} original. Same pixels in every row.
Compare.caveat: Smaller is not automatically better: AVIF and WEBP are unsupported in some older software, and PNG is the only lossless row here.

Crop.metaDescription: Crop JPEG, PNG, WEBP or AVIF images to a preset aspect ratio like 1:1 or 16:9, or a circle with transparent corners, using a draggable crop area.
Crop.heading: Crop
Crop.intro: Pick a preset aspect ratio, then drag the frame to choose exactly what to keep.
Crop.presetHint: Frames that exact ratio and scales the crop to the pixel size the platform expects.
Crop.presetActiveHint: Pick the active preset again to go back to the ratio above.
Crop.circleHint: Keeps only the area inside the ellipse; the corners become transparent. JPEG exports as PNG so the transparency is preserved.
Crop.outputScaled: The {width} × {height} frame is scaled to it.
Crop.dragCorner: Drag the frame to reposition it, or pull a corner to resize.
Crop.dragEdge: Drag the frame to reposition it, or pull an edge or corner to resize.

Convert.metaDescription: Convert images in bulk between JPEG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, TIFF and SVG, build an ICO favicon, or get a Base64 data URI.
Convert.heading: Convert
Convert.intro: Change the format of one image or a batch of 20, or turn the file into a Base64 data URI. Available targets are based on the uploaded files' types.
Convert.detected: {count, plural, one {Detected source format} other {Detected source formats}}: {formats}
Convert.batchNote: Every image gets the same target format. Any file that is already in that format is skipped and reported back.
Convert.svgNote: Embeds the image as a base64-encoded PNG inside an SVG file. The pixels are not traced into vector shapes, so it won't scale beyond the original resolution.
Convert.base64Note: Encodes the image as a data: URI for embedding in CSS or HTML. Best for small images — the text is about a third larger than the file.
Convert.gifNote: Exports a single still frame — animation is not preserved.
Convert.animatedGifNote: If a GIF is animated, only its first frame is converted.
Convert.tiffNote: A lossless format for print and archival. Files are large and most browsers can't preview them.
Convert.icoSizesHint: The .ico holds every selected size as a PNG, fitted on a transparent background; browsers pick the one they need. 16, 32 and 48px cover tabs, bookmarks and the Windows desktop.
Convert.icoPackOn: Bundles favicon.ico with apple-touch-icon.png ({size}px, flattened on white), icon-192.png, icon-512.png, a site.webmanifest and the link tags to paste into the page head.
Convert.icoPackOff: Just the .ico file on its own.
Convert.base64Metadata: If the image carries metadata, removing it re-encodes the pixels, so the embedded bytes differ from the original file. Turn it off to always embed the upload byte-for-byte.
Convert.base64Ready: {count, plural, one {Base64 data URI ready} other {# base64 data URIs ready}}
Convert.truncated: — preview truncated, Copy and Download include the full string.
Convert.generateDataUri: {count, plural, one {Generate data URI} other {Generate data URIs}}

Watermark.metaTitle: Add a watermark to an image
Watermark.metaDescription: Stamp text or a logo onto JPEG, PNG, WEBP or AVIF images — nine positions, adjustable size, margin and opacity, up to 20 images at once.
Watermark.heading: Watermark
Watermark.intro: Stamp your name or your logo onto a batch of photos. The size follows each image's width, so the same settings look right on a thumbnail and on a full-resolution shot.
Watermark.logoHint: A PNG with a transparent background works best — the logo is composited as it is, only scaled and faded.
Watermark.overBudget: The images and the watermark add up to {total} — they travel in one request, which has to stay under {max}.
Watermark.previewHint: Approximate preview of the first image, scaled to fit — the stamp is rendered at full resolution on the download.
Watermark.previewBatch: Every image in the batch gets the same settings, sized to its own width.

Placeholder.metaDescription: Generate solid-color placeholder images with custom dimensions, colors and text as JPEG, PNG, WEBP or AVIF.
Placeholder.heading: Placeholder
Placeholder.intro: Generate a placeholder image with custom dimensions, colors and text — no upload needed.
Placeholder.previewHint: Approximate preview, scaled to fit. The download renders at full size.

ImagesToPdf.metaDescription: Turn JPEG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF or SVG images into a PDF — one page each, sized to fit the image or a standard A4/Letter page.
ImagesToPdf.heading: Images to PDF
ImagesToPdf.intro: Wrap one image in a PDF, or several into a multi-page one, sized to fit the image or a standard page.
ImagesToPdf.batchNote: {images} become {pages} in one PDF, in the order above — use the arrows to rearrange them.

MergePdf.metaDescription: Combine several PDF files into one document, in the order you choose — the pages are copied across without their original titles or authors.
MergePdf.heading: Merge PDFs
MergePdf.intro: Combine several PDFs into one document, in whatever order you arrange them.
MergePdf.needTwo: Add at least one more PDF — merging needs two files.
MergePdf.batchNote: {pdfs} become one document, in the order above — use the arrows to rearrange them. Up to {maxPages} pages in total, and the originals' titles and authors are left behind.

MetadataTool.metaDescription: Read the EXIF, camera, GPS location, color profile and dimensions stored inside JPEG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF images — then download a clean copy with all of it removed.
MetadataTool.heading: Metadata
MetadataTool.intro: Photos carry more than pixels: the camera that took them, when, and often exactly where. Read what is inside yours, then get a copy with none of it.
MetadataTool.privacyNote: Nothing is uploaded until you press the button, and the file is read in memory and dropped — the report is built on the server and sent straight back.
MetadataTool.readFailed: Could not read the metadata report.
MetadataTool.removableSome: {count} of {files} {count, plural, one {carries} other {carry}} removable metadata
MetadataTool.removableHint: A clean copy is re-encoded without EXIF, GPS, ICC or XMP. The orientation is baked into the pixels first, so the photo cannot come out sideways. Files that carry nothing are reported back instead of copied.

Metadata.gpsTitle: This photo knows where it was taken
Metadata.gpsBody: GPS coordinates {coordinates} travel inside the file. Anyone you send it to can read them.

MetadataSwitch.label: Remove metadata (EXIF, GPS location, ICC, XMP)
MetadataSwitch.on: Strips all embedded metadata from the output, including GPS location.
MetadataSwitch.off: Keeps the original metadata in the output file.
